$comment: The bare field name released in ui 0.3.0 and 0.4.0 named a field of the array entry enclosing the context; that entry is the object holding the field the region is declared on whenever the region sits on a field of an array entry, which is every published use, so the bare name is exactly the pointer `0/<name>`. `valuePattern` admits only a bare name, so a pointer — or anything else — is left for the validator. `inSchema` with the wildcard `inKind` / `under` reaches the annotation wherever a kind or a named shape writes it, and `notUnder` keeps the rule out of data-bearing keywords.
reason: `x-telo-context-element-from-item` names the field whose chain types the binding with a relative JSON pointer from the object holding the field the region is declared on (`0/rows` for a sibling, `2/rows` two levels up), so a region on a list column's own field can reach the list's `rows`; a bare field name could name only a field of the enclosing array entry.
